key_insight: Hydrogen-free route to single-crystal-quality p- and n-FETs inside the stack: the fallback that de-risks Smart Cut's implanted hydrogen for in-stack sense amps (I-11545).
killer_doubt: Delft grains (3-7.5 um) were shown with ~1 um-gate devices. Sense-amp pairs need <=20 mV mismatch at ~0.1 um in twinned grains. Floating-body Z-RAM failed even on crystalline SOI.
decisive_experiment: Sputter Si over a finished 2-tier IGZO TFT stack (0.7 um SiO2 buffer, grain filters). Laser-crystallize with Delft's tool, then build 0.1-0.25 um n/p FETs and SA pairs. Measure mismatch, Ioff, and underlying IGZO Vt shift. ~$350k.
prior_art: Delft mu-Czochralski single-grain TFTs, including a 2-layer 3D CMOS inverter and 6T-SRAM (prior logs); CEA-Leti 400 C ns-laser CMOS; Z-RAM floating body [training knowledge].

key_insight: In memory-on-logic stacks the memory tier can sit next to the coolant. 1 W/mm2 across 50 um of Si costs only ~0.3 K, so memory runs ~10-30 K above water.
killer_doubt: Refresh is ~10-20% of power and bandwidth, so an 8x cut buys ~10-15% at system level. A tail-cell activation energy of ~0.3-0.6 eV may cap the retention gain at 3-10x.
decisive_experiment: Thermal-chuck retention-tail maps of commodity DDR5/LPDDR5 dies at 45, 65 and 85 C on an FPGA tester, extracting the tail activation energy, plus a thermal model of a bonded microchannel stack. ~$80k.
prior_art: Microsoft/Corintis in-silicon microfluidics (2025, prior logs); IBM CMOSAIC interlayer 3D-IC cooling; Liu et al. ISCA 2013 retention vs temperature; same family as dropped I-11571.

key_insight: Even at 1-2 b/cell, 8-16 oxide tiers over an 800 mm2 logic die hold ~25-100 GB at ~0.2 pJ/bit with no extra wafer: HBM-stack capacity without the TSV tax.
killer_doubt: Memory yield multiplies into a ~$25k logic wafer: 1% loss per tier is ~15% at 16 tiers. 3-bit levels sit ~140 mV apart, near expected 95 C PBTI drift.
decisive_experiment: 4-tier vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C arrays (64 kb) on finished 65-130 nm foundry CMOS wafers. Measure 2-3 b retention and Vt drift at 95-105 C across 1e9 write-verify cycles, plus logic ring-oscillator shift. ~$600k.
prior_art: TSMC fully-BEOL oxide-selector memory over logic (VLSI 2025); CXMT BEOL multi-layer IGZO DRAM (IEDM 2025); imec BEOL 2T0C IGZO eDRAM; NUS all-BEOL 2T0C.

key_insight: With plane-major weight storage, one model serves its own 2-4-bit draft from the same bytes, so speculative decoding needs no second model and no extra capacity.
killer_doubt: Gain is capped at 1.1-1.8x. Each draft token still reads 25-50% of the weight bytes, and SpecMQuant found that verification compute cancels 4-bit memory savings. A niche software gain.
decisive_experiment: On one GPU, quantize Llama-3-8B/70B with MatGPTQ and store the weights plane-major. Measure acceptance rate and bytes per accepted token for 2- and 4-plane drafts against EAGLE-style drafters. ~$30k.
prior_art: Matryoshka Quantization (ICML 2025), MatGPTQ, SpecMQuant (via search snippet); Any-Precision LLM bit-plane serving; QSpec/QuantSpec quantized self-speculation [training knowledge].

key_insight: When density comes from tiers rather than pitch, F~100 nm is acceptable, so imprint and display-class litho could in principle replace EUV for 3D oxide memory.
killer_doubt: 3D memory capital is HAR etch and deposition (roughly half of 3D NAND tool spend), not litho. No panel HAR-etch tool exists; 64-128 tiers (~3-13 um film) warp glass.
decisive_experiment: Deposit a 32-pair oxide/nitride stack on 370x470 mm Gen-2 glass at a display R&D line. Map bow, stress and imprint-overlay residuals across the panel, then cost-model a panel HAR-etch tool. ~$400k.
prior_art: Large-glass imprinted wire-grid polarizers at 100-200 nm (prior logs); Kioxia/Canon NIL for NAND. No display-line DRAM found (R17 search).

key_insight: Split keys by bit significance and the sketch is the real data's MSB planes: PIM scores tokens in place, the GPU fetches only top-k, full KV moves to cheaper tiers.
killer_doubt: GPU-side quantized or low-rank key sketches (ShadowKV, Quest, SparQ) already save ~5-7x KV without PIM. PIM availability, and whether 4-bit-key top-k recall reaches ~95%, are undecided.
decisive_experiment: GPU emulation at 128k tokens on RULER/LongBench with Llama-3.1-8B. Compare top-k recall and accuracy of 4-MSB-plane key scores against full keys and ShadowKV, then model PIM timing from LPDDR5X-PIM specs. ~$60k.
prior_art: Quest, SparQ, InfiniGen, ShadowKV [training knowledge]; StarC PIM selective-token access and hybrid-bonded near-memory top-k (prior logs); KIVI; Samsung LPDDR5X-PIM.

key_insight: Capping vertical bitlines at 16 cells (~2-4 fF) cuts the needed Cs to ~0.3-0.6 fF, shrinking the 3D capacitor ~10-20x: the reading-is-solved insight applied inside the stack.
killer_doubt: Each 16-tier group adds a bonded donor layer and ~15-25 low-temperature CMOS masks, perhaps ~$3-6k per wafer for 4 groups. <=400 C FETs and implant hydrogen threaten IGZO tiers.
decisive_experiment: With CEA-Leti or a Smart-Cut university partner, bond and split c-Si over a 4-tier IGZO TFT stack with an Al2O3/SiN barrier. Measure IGZO Vt shift (<20 mV target), Ioff, and the quality of ns-laser n/p FETs. ~$700k.
prior_art: Samsung 16-tier VS-DRAM with bonded peri-on-cell (VLSI 2026); CEA-Leti CoolCube and 400 C sequential CMOS; Monolithic 3D Inc. ion-cut 3D-memory patents [training knowledge].

key_insight: Binary Vt-coded select regions decode N tiers with 2*log2(N) pillars (12 at 64 tiers), so line ends shrink ~12x and short, sub-page 3D DRAM lines become area-affordable.
killer_doubt: Each line crosses 12 series oxide select devices (~30 kOhm each, ~0.4 MOhm total). Unselected-tier wordlines float instead of being held at a rail, inviting coupling disturb and leakage.
decisive_experiment: 8-tier IGZO TFT stack with coded depletion/enhancement select regions (block-mask doping or charge-trap programming). Measure series resistance, line RC, and unselected-line float drift and disturb at 85 C, plus SPICE of 64-tier decode. ~$350k.
prior_art: Macronix VG-NAND layer selection by programmed select gates (LSM); NMOS depletion/enhancement-coded ROM decoders (1970s-80s) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Programmable tier decode makes tier-level sparing cheap (~6% area), and the arithmetic is right: 0.99^64 is about 53%, so 3D DRAM needs some tier redundancy.
killer_doubt: Dominant 3D defects (blocked or bowed HAR holes) are vertical and kill every tier of a string, which tier spares miss. Pre-tested 8-tier groups need 8 substrates per stack.
decisive_experiment: Desk study: a yield model fed with the published 3D NAND defect Pareto (vertical vs per-tier), plus a cost model of 1 vs 8 substrates. ~$20k, folded into the I-11545 dossier.
prior_art: DRAM row/column redundancy; 3D NAND bad-block and wordline management; HBM known-good-die and spare TSVs [training knowledge].

key_insight: Vacuum is a barrier with no traps: write current through it cannot cause SILC or breakdown. That makes it one of the triage's four routes to DRAM-class write endurance.
killer_doubt: Write current shifts ~2x and retention ~9x per 0.1 nm of gap. ns writes need ~6 V/nm local fields (~160 MPa pressure), where field-driven atom migration may reshape gaps.
decisive_experiment: In a university nanofab, make lateral TiN/vacuum/TiN gaps of 2.5-4 nm by ALD Al2O3 sacrificial release and seal. Measure gap spread over 1e4 devices, FN I-V, and drift over 1e10 10-ns cycles. ~$400k.
prior_art: None found for vacuum-gap floating gates (via search snippet). Related: NASA Ames vacuum-channel transistors (prior logs); AIST/Funai nanogap resistive switches [training knowledge].

key_insight: Deposition-only charge-shift strings remove the per-bit transistor, capacitor and EUV, and wide-gap oxide channels hold packets with no dark current: block-access density at 3D NAND cost.
killer_doubt: Bit 64 needs ~128 gate transfers, so at imec's CTE of 98% (if per transfer) only ~7% survives. DRAM-class needs >=0.9999, clocked ~100x faster than imec's 4-6 MHz.
decisive_experiment: 32-64-plane vertical IGZO CCD pillars through imec IIAP or a university fab. Measure per-transfer CTE against clock (5-200 MHz) and temperature, and packet loss after 128 transfers. ~$600k.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD: planar 142-bit (IEDM 2024, CTE >98%) and vertical 3D CCD (IMW 2026) for CXL buffer (prior logs). Same family as N-08/I-05275.

key_insight: Reuses DRAM's 60:1 hole as a 10-25-bit magnetic shift register. Magnetic order has no write wear-out and needs no refresh, and modulated wires grow cheaply in AAO templates.
killer_doubt: Cylindrical-wire experiments show stochastic pinning, yet DRAM needs shift errors <1e-12 per shift at ~1e7 A/cm2. 20 nm MTJs at 35-40 nm pitch are ~2x tighter than production MRAM.
decisive_experiment: Electroplate Co/Ni-modulated 20-40 nm wires (60 nm period) in AAO templates. Contact single wires and measure the current-driven shift error rate over 1e8 pulses by magnetoresistance at 300-360 K. ~$350k.
prior_art: IBM Parkin vertical racetrack proposal (Science 2008); Schobitz et al. 2019 Bloch-point walls >600 m/s; Madrid modulated-wire pinning studies (prior logs).
